title: The Alexander family and violinist Pete Alexander
summary: Pete Alexander, Tats Alexander and their father, who led a big brass band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Fiddlers and reading violinists of New Orleans

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, you already talk, that fella, Louis Double, Red Allen. Oh, yeah. I played with all them, yeah. George O'Neill. Yeah. George O'Neill, he's not here though. Now, they got an old friend of mine, he used to play violin. He used to play with Sam Morgan and them, but he stopped playing years. I know some of them old fellas too, but he stopped playing years. He's a violin player? He used to play violin, yeah. What is his name? Pete Alexander. Oh, Pete Alexander.
And I know of course Tats, Adolph Alexander, any relation to them? No, I played with Tats, but he's kind of paralyzed. Yeah, he had a sort of stroke.
I played many times with Tats, yeah. He's paralyzed now.
Good musician. He played baritone horn too, I know. His dad used to be a teacher. Old man Alexander. I used to play at that big band, Heard Talk of Pritchett. Yeah.
But he couldn't get them fellas to play it.
I know why they didn't want to learn you. He had a good band. It was a big brass band, wasn't it? Big brass band.
